title: Quality Bound
description: Schema for quality bound specifications in the PROJ-036 Prompt Regression Test Harness. Quality bounds define the acceptable score ranges per agent per evaluation dimension using the S-014 six-dimension rubric from quality-enforcement.md. These are probabilistic expectations, not hard Boolean invariants.

agent.description: The agent identifier this quality bound applies to.

version.description: Contract version for this quality bound specification.

overall_floor.description: Minimum acceptable S-014 composite score expected from a well-functioning agent on a standard task (mean across N=30 runs). Scores below this floor across N >= 20 runs (Wilson score lower bound) indicate systematic underperformance and trigger QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH.

minimum_acceptable.description: Absolute minimum composite score (overall_floor minus tolerance). Below this value, even the Wilson score lower bound triggers QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH. Typically overall_floor - 0.04.

max_composite_std_dev.description: Maximum acceptable standard deviation for composite quality scores across N=30 runs of identical prompts. Exceeding this threshold indicates the prompt is under-constrained and produces unstable quality.

max_dimension_std_dev.description: Maximum acceptable standard deviation for any individual S-014 dimension score across N=30 runs. Must be >= max_composite_std_dev (dimension variance can exceed composite variance due to averaging).

max_cv.description: Maximum acceptable coefficient of variation (CV = std_dev / mean) for composite scores. CV > 0.10 triggers STABILITY_WARNING. Default: 0.10.

per_dimension.description: Per-dimension score bounds for each of the six S-014 evaluation dimensions. All six dimensions must be specified.

completeness.description: Bound for the Completeness dimension (weight: 0.20). All necessary information must be present; nothing essential is omitted.

internal_consistency.description: Bound for the Internal Consistency dimension (weight: 0.20). No conflicting statements; conclusions follow from evidence.

methodological_rigor.description: Bound for the Methodological Rigor dimension (weight: 0.20). Appropriate methods applied correctly; reasoning is sound.

evidence_quality.description: Bound for the Evidence Quality dimension (weight: 0.15). Claims are supported; sources are authoritative and cited.

actionability.description: Bound for the Actionability dimension (weight: 0.15). Output can be acted upon; recommendations are concrete.

traceability.description: Bound for the Traceability dimension (weight: 0.10). Claims trace to sources; reasoning chain is visible.

band_thresholds.description: Quality band classification thresholds per quality-enforcement.md H-13. These must align with the universal thresholds; agent-specific overrides are NOT permitted for PASS/REVISE boundaries (they are set by the Jerry Constitution).

pass_minimum.description: Minimum score for PASS classification. Must be 0.92 per quality-enforcement.md H-13. This field exists for documentation; any value other than 0.92 is a contract error.

revise_minimum.description: Minimum score for REVISE classification (below PASS, above REJECTED). Must be 0.85 per quality-enforcement.md.

rejected_maximum.description: Maximum score for REJECTED classification (exclusive). Must be 0.85 per quality-enforcement.md.

floor_breach_detection.description: Configuration for QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH detection using Wilson score intervals.

wilson_confidence_level.description: Confidence level for Wilson score interval calculation.

minimum_n_for_floor_check.description: Minimum sample size required before Wilson-based floor check is applied.

rationale.description: Documented rationale for the quality floor and dimension bounds for this agent.

floor_rationale.description: Explanation of why this agent's quality floor is set at its specified value.

differentiation_from_universal.description: Explanation of how this agent's bounds differ from other agents and why.

key_dimension_notes.description: Optional per-dimension notes explaining bounds for specific dimensions.

source.description: Reference to the behavioral-contracts.md section that defines this quality bound.

dimension_bound.description: Score range specification for a single S-014 dimension.

min.description: Minimum expected score for this dimension. Scores consistently below this minimum (across N >= 20 runs) trigger DIMENSION_FLOOR_WARNING.

max.description: Maximum expected score for this dimension. Scores above this maximum are unexpected but not penalized (max is used for anomaly detection only).
max.const_note: Should be 1.0 in most cases; only lower if there is a principled reason why the agent cannot achieve perfect scores on this dimension.

rationale.description: Optional dimension-specific rationale for why the bounds are set at these values.

completeness.rationale: All 6 S-014 dimensions must be scored; incomplete scoring is a hard failure covered by SI-SCOR-002

internal_consistency.rationale: Arithmetic consistency between dimension scores and composite is required

methodological_rigor.rationale: Systematic rubric application; highest rigor expectation among all agents

evidence_quality.rationale: Scores must cite artifact evidence; not purely impressionistic

actionability.rationale: Scores must enable quality gate decisions; PASS/REVISE/REJECTED must be stated

traceability.rationale: Every score must trace to a specific rubric criterion

rationale.floor_rationale: adv-scorer applies a systematic rubric to a fixed set of dimensions. This is the most constrained task among the five target agents: the rubric is defined, the dimensions are known, and the scoring criteria are explicit. Higher floor (0.90) reflects this reduced task variability.
rationale.differentiation_from_universal: adv-scorer's floor is 0.08 above ps-researcher's (0.82) because adv-scorer operates on a fixed rubric rather than open-ended research. Systematic tasks with clear criteria should produce higher and more consistent quality scores.

key_dimension_notes.methodological_rigor: adv-scorer's primary function is rubric application; this dimension reflects core competency
key_dimension_notes.traceability: Score rationale must be visible and traceable to rubric criteria; this is a primary output requirement
